messages:
ops-oncall: ALARM - mel1 control plane is silent, provisioning API failing, autoscaler queuing tasks but nothing gets scheduled. Seeing 504s from region gateway. :rotating_light:
monitoring-bot: [alert] mel1: api-lb 95% 504s, kube-apiserver 0/3 endpoints healthy, provisioning queue length +1200 in last 2m.
mia: on it, pulling logs and kube API status. first check: cannot curl https://mel1-api.internal/healthz -> connection timed out.
sam: I can still SSH to some bastions in mel1, but node agent heartbeats stopped at ~1959991080.
infra-eng: confirming: our control-plane VMs show kernel network flaps in serial logs, kubelet processes OOM-killed on multiple hosts. looks like sudden memory pressure on controller nodes.
neteng: cloud provider reports packet loss on the regional fabric since ~1959991055, opened ticket CR-8421. They claim routing plane was degraded during a rolling upgrade.
ops-oncall: impact? which customers affected?
nina: approx 30% of live inference traffic in APAC was pinned to mel1 by smart-routing; requests are failing or timing out. No data plane failover triggered because backend health false-negative due to API errors.
sam: autoscaler stuck because control plane not accepting new pods. we need to force traffic shift at edge to avoid hit.
mia: suggested quick mitigation: 1) set route policy to prefer ap-southeast1 / ap-northeast1 for mel1 prefixes, 2) enable emergency capacity in other regions, 3) start forced evacuation of stateful pods.
ops-oncall: Agreed. Initiating traffic shift. @deploy-bot kick off edge reroute: set weight mel1=0, ap-southeast1=70, ap-northeast1=30.
deploy-bot: edge-reroute job queued. running: set-weight --prefix=mel1 --weights "ap-southeast1:70,ap-northeast1:30".
deploy-bot: done. propagation ~30s.
monitoring-bot: edge: mel1 traffic drop -> 0.8% within 40s. errors to customer shrink.
neteng: adding static BGP withdraws for affected prefixes to reduce noisy retransmits. Doing withdraws now.
infra-eng: starting emergency restart of controller VMs one-by-one with constrained memory cgroups to avoid OOM. Command: ``for i in controllers; do ssh $i sudo systemctl restart kube-apiserver && sleep 20; done``
ops-oncall: good. While infra-eng works on controllers, runbook action items: A) Keep traffic shifted until control plane stable B) Validate KV store consistency C) Evacuate provision queue by replay to other regions.
mia: I dumped etcd leader status: leader present but followers lagging ~30s. Will snapshot and replicate to cold storage.
sam: provisioning queue replay: we can take queued tasks from mel1 and resubmit to global-queue with region_hint. I'll start that with throttling so we don't spike other regions.
ops-oncall: estimate time to partial recovery?
infra-eng: after controller restarts we expect API to accept requests within ~3-5 minutes if no deeper corruption. If etcd has compaction issues, could be longer.
nina: communicating to support: telling customers of degraded service and that we are actively shifting traffic and will update in 30m.
sam: running health checks: ``kubectl --context=mel1 get nodes --no-headers | awk '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c`` -> most nodes in NotReady state.
ops-oncall: escalate to Exec on-call if >30m. tagging @cto for visibility.
neteng: cloud provider status page now shows 'degraded networking' and they flagged a rolling fabric upgrade as root cause; they expect full remediation by 1959991600.
infra-eng: continuing controlled restarts. snapshots done. etctd leader election stable. starting to accept new schedules -> beginning to drain the provisioning queue by replaying to other regions.
mia: Post-mortem notes to capture: provider rolling upgrade impact, missing graceful fallback for control-plane-only failures, autoscaler dependency on API health, and runbook clarity on forced edge reroutes.
ops-oncall: summary (initial triage): 1) Root cause: regional network fabric upgrade causing packet loss -> controller OOMs and kube API silence. 2) Impact: mel1 full control-plane outage -> provisioning and API 504s, ~30% APAC traffic affected. 3) Mitigation: edge reroute to other regions, BGP withdraws, controller restarts, queue replay. 4) Next steps: full recovery verification, customer comms, postmortem.
nina: adding scheduled update at +15m.
ops-oncall: closing thread for initial triage, will reopen if conditions change. :white_check_mark:
